result.summary: Ensure block data I/O errors are handled cleanly instead of being silently swallowed or triggering hard assertions. It updates FlatFileSeq::Open so that parent directory creation failures return nullptr rather than throwing an unhandled filesystem exception, and replaces an assert in GETBLOCKTXN message handling with a fatal graceful shutdown. Extensive unit and functional tests are added to verify filesystem failure behavior across block connection, reorgs, RPCs, and P2P requests.
result.problem: When the blocks directory becomes inaccessible (such as during a detached storage volume or permissions change), FlatFileSeq::Open throws a filesystem_error. When this occurs during ActivateBestChain, the exception bypasses FatalError and is swallowed by the generic P2P catch-all with only net-debug logging, leaving the node appearing alive but permanently stuck and unable to advance the chain. Additionally, GETBLOCKTXN crashes via assertion on read errors instead of initiating a graceful shutdown.
evidence: PR description: 'If it happens during block connection (due to the unguarded FlatFileSeq::Open -> fs::create_directories call), after AcceptBlock(), inside ActivateBestChain(), the error gets thrown and swallowed by the P2P general try-catch, leaving the node in a living but stuck state.'

Commit 8a3ec93d54: 'swallowing the error msg for any regular user, and every subsequent block arrival retries the same failing read, leaving the node looking healthy while the block processing mechanism is stuck.'
result.scope_notes: The production code change is only around 15 lines across src/flatfile.cpp and src/net_processing.cpp; the vast majority of the patch is test infrastructure and test cases simulating filesystem I/O failures.
result.changed_since_previous: The code and functional scope remain the same; only minor test adjustments or rebase updates distinguish this patch from the previous version.
result.card: PR 35003 ensures that block data I/O failures do not silently stall block processing or trigger abrupt assertions. If the block directory becomes inaccessible, FlatFileSeq::Open previously threw an exception that was swallowed by the P2P thread catch-all, leaving nodes running but stuck unable to connect new blocks. It changes FlatFileSeq::Open to return null on directory creation failure, changes GETBLOCKTXN read failures from an assertion abort to a graceful fatal error shutdown, and adds extensive functional and unit test coverage for disk access failures.

risk.why: Modifies core file access logic in FlatFileSeq used by block storage and changes shutdown signaling during P2P message handling.
